newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's RHB Sakura boosts shareholders' funds.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's RHB Sakura boosts shareholders' funds.

text.p: Malaysia's RHB Sakura Merchant Bankers Bhd said on Monday that it has raised its shareholders' funds to 566 million ringgit from 327 million.

RHB Sakura chairman Abdul Rashid Hussain said the increase will allow the company to undertake more banking and capital market investment and underwriting activities, and also allow it to expand regionally.

"Earlier today, following a cash subscription, the bank's consolidated shareholders' funds have increased by 239 million ringgit to a proforma level of 566 milion ringgit based on its balance sheet as at December 31, 1996," he said in a speech at the bank's underwriting signing ceremony.
The move also increased the bank's risk-weighted capital adequacy position from 10.3 percent to about 17 percent as at end-December last year, he said.
RHB Sakura, formerly known as DCB Sakura Merchant Bankers Bhd, is making a public offer for sale of 28.36 million shares at 4.10 ringgit each.
The bank plans to list on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange in mid-August, Abdul Rashid told reporters after the signing ceremony.
He said RHB Capital's stake in RHB Sakura will be reduced to 51 percent after the public share offer and a restricted sale of 50.88 million shares at 4.10 ringgit each.
RHB Sakura is currently a wholly-owned unit of RHB Capital, formerly DCB Holdings Bhd.
Abdul Rashid himself will hold a 20 percent stake in the enlarged share capital of RHB Sakura of 338.66 million shares.
Other staff members of the merchant bank and the public will hold the remaining 29 percent stake.

RHB Sakura reported pretax profit of 106.7 million ringgit in the year ended December 31, 1996, with total assets of 4.5 billion ringgit, making it the second largest merchant bank in Malaysia after Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank.
